data.source_title: The impact of a multimodal intervention on emergency department crowding and patient flow
data.locator: Table 8, “Overall (24/7) radiology report turnaround times”; Methods, Study design and intervention; Results.
data.source_setting: Haaglanden Medical Center Westeinde, inner-city 380-bed acute neurovascular/level 1 trauma center, Netherlands; annual ED census 54,000; GP-cooperative referrals excluded.
data.source_period: 9-month pre-intervention period Dec 2016–Sep 2017 and 9-month intervention period Dec 2017–Sep 2018, as stated by authors; 18 months total.
data.source_n: Table 8 period counts sum to 40,769 radiology orders (20,082 pre + 20,687 intervention); the paper states turnaround values were missing for 99 orders, leaving 40,670 nonmissing turnaround observations. Included ED presentations: 64,012 (31,891 pre, 32,121 intervention).
data.quantity: All radiology report turnaround time, median (IQR), before and during multimodal intervention
data.source_evidence_basis: Observed order-level hospital information-system intervals, reported as median (IQR); Table 8 explicitly says overall 24/7 and is based on orders with missing values excluded.
data.limitations: Single site; nonrandomized before/after comparison with four simultaneous workflow changes (including radiology Lean work), so change cannot be attributed to any one intervention. Patient population and construction conditions differed over time.
data.inferred_scenario_use: External benchmark for overall order-to-radiology-report interval and sensitivity scenario; intervention contrast is descriptive and not a guaranteed treatment effect. Keep ED LOS separate from report turnaround.
